newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Tender process for Ukraine's AvtoZAZ continues.
newsitem.headline: Tender process for Ukraine's AvtoZAZ continues.

text.p: The tender process for Ukraine's AvtoZAZ carmaker is continuing and local media reports that South Korea's Daewoo had reached agreement to modernise the plant to build vehicles there are premature, the president's adviser on the economy said.
"There is still a tender going on for AvtoZAZ," Valery Lytvytsky told Reuters on Thursday.

General Motors Corp of the U.S. is due to complete a feasibility study, partially funded by the U.S. government, to determine whether it could manufacture jointly with the eastern Ukrainian car builder.
Ukrainian media reported after a Thursday meeting with Daewoo and President Leonid Kuchma that Daewoo was prepared to invest more than $1 billion in AvtoZAZ, maker of the Tavria mid-range car.
"A strategic agreement about the participation of Daewoo in the reconstruction of our automobile plant and the beginning of dual manufacture was accepted," the official DINAU news agency said.
It added that 300,000 vehicles would be built annually.
Daewoo's chief Ukraine representative would not comment on the reports.
"There are many ongoing projects by Daewoo in Ukraine," Jae Ho Kim said. "I'd rather have all things announced from the government side."
DINAU said the two sides also discussed Daewoo's modernisation of electronics factories in Ukraine.
The company announced this month participation in a $200 million joint venture with the city of Kiev to build a business centre in the capital.
Kuchma paid a state visit to South Korea earlier this month.
